newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE ends higher as bonds, Eurobourses, surge.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE ends higher as bonds, Eurobourses, surge.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE closes higher, bolstered by advancing bonds and
sharp gains on Eurobourses amid strengthening dollar.
** Pressure from sterling caps gains. Dow up 27 points.
** Barclays advances on renewed buyback hopes. Stores sector
gains on rising consumer demand ahead of Christmas.
"The U.S. is open but only for a half day and we are trading higher on the back of the bond markets," said the head of equity trading at one leading brokerage.

Traders said Friday's rise in leading stockmarkets was driven by a stronger dollar sparking renewed hopes for lower interest rates in continental Europe. Gilts and German government bunds lent support. The December long gilt future climbed to a new contract high of 111-27/32 up 28/32 on the day.
Germany's Dax leapt to a record high for a second day, after comments from a Bank of France official in favour of a stronger dollar, hinting that European interest rates may have to fall.
Yet the FTSE underperformed other markets, as the strength of sterling -- which reached a 33-month high against the mark -- weighed down on the export prospects of major international stocks.
Imperial Chemical Industries lost 10-1/2p to 769-1/2p and British Steel was down 3-1/4p at 166p.

Trading volumes were modest with 564 million shares changing hands. Second-line stocks were also mostly higher with the FTSE 250 up 11.8 points at 4,428.0 and the Reuters-HSBC 150 index of the leading 150 stocks up 2.51 points at 1,097.47.
In the meantime there were hopes that the FTSE, which on Tuesday touched an intraday record high of 4,094.4, was still set for its traditional year-end rally.

"My feeling is this market wants to go better," said one dealer. "The market is nervous but with fund managers holding plenty of cash the likelihood is it will respond more to good news rather than bad."

Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming, said the bond market rally was a bullish sign. "The market is trying to rally and we could break 4,100 next week," he said. "If we break 4,100 I think we will see a quick advance in December."

In New York, where the Dow's recent record breaking performance has been supporting London stocks, the market was due to shut at 1800 GMT in a carryover from Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday. As London markets closed, the Dow was up 27 points but traders said activity was thin.
Elsewhere, HTV finished 20p higher at 372p after United News & Media confirmed it had increased its stake to 29.9 percent. United News shares were up 11p at 676-1/2.
Argos was up 14p at 773-1/2p amid buoyant consumer demand. Meanwhile, Great Universal Stores put on 18p to 685-1/2p and Kingfisher was up 16p at 648-1/2p ahead of results next week.
Schroders was another strong feature, up 50p at 15.25 stg as a large block of shares in the tightly-held stock was traded in the market.

Shares in Land Securities were up 9p at 738-1/2p after analysts at HSBC James Capel repeated their positive stance on the stock, traders said. Barclays reached a record 10.30 stg amid renewed hopes for a share buyback from the cash-rich banking group but later eased to close at 10.24-1/2.
Whitbread made a late rally, rising to a record high after NatWest repeated an "add" recommendation on the stock. The shares finished at 765-1/2p, up 10p on the day.
-- Elaine Hardcastle, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
